tools.name: check_incentives
tools.description: Clean-energy incentive source guidance by country and postal code; eligibility is not verified. US ZIP → federal status + state/utility programs (via DSIRE). Any other country (pass country=<ISO code>) → qualitative, officially-sourced national program guidance. Use whenever a user asks what rebates

tools.name: estimate_production
tools.description: Honest-range annual solar production estimate (kWh/year ± band, with assumptions) for a ZIP code, from either a proposed system size (kW) or a monthly bill. Use to sanity-check installer quotes or size a system before talking to anyone. Inputs: zipCode, country, systemKw, monthlyBillUsd. Cost: free

tools.name: get_node_score
tools.description: Instant Energy Node Score (0–100 across 7 axes: efficiency, electrification, renewable generation, storage/resilience, financial optimization, carbon, market readiness) plus the single highest-leverage next action, from whatever property facts you have. More inputs → tighter score. Inputs: zipCode,

tools.name: get_quote_link
tools.description: Optional household handoff: returns a free assessment URL and a separate $49 founding Quote Guardian human-review offer for a solar, battery or heat-pump proposal. For an automated agent result, use review_installer_quote on the full MCP endpoint. Share a household service only when it fits the user

tools.name: get_power_passport_link
tools.description: Qualify the minimum non-sensitive project facts for EnergyAI’s $2,500 founding Power Passport and return an attributable website handoff plus ready-to-paste shareText. Use when a compute, data-center, renewable-energy, utility, or infrastructure buyer needs a five-business-day pre-feasibility screen

tools.name: get_power_service_quote
tools.description: Create a signed, 15-minute, scope-bound quote for EnergyAI’s $1 Power Screen from non-sensitive site and workload facts. Returns the quoteToken required by run_power_screen, exact price, evidence boundary, authorization class, and higher-tier handoffs. Free and never spends funds. Inputs: siteLocati

tools.name: route_lead
tools.description: Submit a consented homeowner project to EnergyAI’s guarded installer-matching workflow — free to you and the homeowner. EnergyAI immediately screens and routes currently available approved installers; unmatched projects remain recorded for safety-controlled follow-up. REQUIRES the homeowner’s explic

tools.name: list_guides
tools.description: Index of source-cited, US home-energy incentive guides with source links (solar, heat pumps, batteries, weatherization) by state. Free. Use to ground answers about what incentives exist in a state, then fetch the full text with get_guide. Every entry includes a canonical URL you can cite. Inputs: re

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Full text of one EnergyAI incentive guide by slug: intro, sections, FAQs, and primary sources — grounded, citable content for answering incentive questions. Free. Harmless slug aliases resolve automatically; genuinely missing topics return grounded guidance and suggestions, and distinct-caller deman

tools.name: create_builder_key
tools.description: Create an EnergyAI production API key in-band with no browser or card after the human operator has authorized the Terms and Privacy Policy. Returns a live key plus three commercial trial calls. Attach the key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` to this MCP endpoint and start with review_installer_quote

tools.name: get_builder_upgrade_link
tools.description: Returns the revenue handoff for EnergyAI Builder. With a key, it returns a PAYABLE Stripe link plus ready-to-paste shareText for the $19/month plan with $20 monthly tool credit, or a prepaid top-up. Without a key, it returns one first-party activation URL where the human enters name and email, accep

tools.name: find_local_installers
tools.description: Publicly-rated local clean-energy contractors for a US ZIP or state (solar, battery, EV charger, heat pump, weatherization, audits), with rating and review count. Free. Use when a homeowner asks WHO can do the work near them. IMPORTANT: results include a listingStatus per company and a disclosure fi

tools.name: energy_calendar
tools.description: Energy Odds (paper mode): upcoming target dates for three public EIA numbers (US retail gasoline weekly, US commercial crude inventories weekly, Henry Hub weekly high/low), EIA release timing, and whether a forecast is already logged for each date. Free. Inputs: series. Cost: always free, no key nee

tools.name: energy_forecast
tools.description: Energy Odds (paper mode, free): the forecast logged in advance for a public EIA number and target date: median, 5/25/50/75/95% quantiles, probabilities above thresholds, model version, EIA inputs with timestamps, forecast_id and hash. Never computed on request: if nothing was logged it returns not_f

tools.name: energy_track_record
tools.description: Energy Odds public track record, free forever: per series counts, Brier score, CRPS, calibration bins and the same scores for two simple baselines, plus the go-paid gate result and its reasons. Inputs: series. Cost: always free, no key needed. Example: {} [always free — no API key required]

tools.name: check_quote_red_flags
tools.description: Free automated check of an installer quote for solar, a battery or a heat pump, from its key numbers: price, system size, equipment, incentives claimed, warranty and state. Returns up to 5 red flags (expired federal credits counted, price per watt outside the usual range, missing workmanship warrant

tools.name: verify_forecast
tools.description: Verify an Energy Odds forecast, free forever: recomputes the hash chain up to that record and returns whether it is intact, when it was logged, its cutoff, and whether it was logged before the cutoff. Inputs: forecast_id (required). Cost: always free, no key needed. Example: {"forecast_id":"us_crude

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "solar" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_quote_link, get_power_passport_link, list_guides, get_guide, get_builder_upgrade_link, check_quote_red_flags · Private data: get_quote_link, get_power_passport_link, get_power_service_quote, route_lead, create_builder_key, get_builder_upgrade_link, find_local_installers, energy_calendar, energy_forecast, energy_track_record, check_quote_red_flags, verify_forecast · Public sink: get_quote_link, route_lead, get_builder_upgrade_link, check_quote_red_flags.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_quote_link, get_power_passport_link, list_guides, get_guide, get_builder_upgrade_link, check_quote_red_flags · Private data: get_quote_link, get_power_passport_link, get_power_service_quote, route_lead, create_builder_key, get_builder_upgrade_link, find_local_installers, energy_calendar, energy_forecast, energy_track_record, check_quote_red_flags, verify_forecast · Public sink: get_quote_link, route_lead, get_builder_upgrade_link, check_quote_red_flags

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
